concepts.name: Arabic letters and sounds
concepts.summary: Recognise and pronounce the 28 letters, including emphatic and guttural sounds like ع, ح, ق, ص and ط.

concepts.name: Right-to-left connected script
concepts.summary: Explain that Arabic is written right to left and that most letters join to the following letter, with six non-connecting letters.

concepts.name: Positional letter forms
concepts.summary: Recognise the isolated, initial, medial and final shapes of a letter and identify the same letter in each position.

concepts.name: Short vowels and harakat
concepts.summary: Read fatha, damma and kasra, plus sukun and shadda, and understand that they are usually omitted in ordinary texts.

concepts.name: Long vowels and madd letters
concepts.summary: Distinguish the long vowels ā, ū, ī written with ا, و, ي from the short vowels and from the consonant uses of و and ي.

concepts.name: Definite article al-
concepts.summary: Use ال to make nouns definite and know that Arabic has no indefinite article.

concepts.name: Sun and moon letters
concepts.summary: Predict when the lam of al- assimilates to the following letter, as in ash-shams, and when it does not, as in al-qamar.

concepts.name: Gender and basic greetings
concepts.summary: Recognise the feminine ending ة and use common greetings such as salām and marḥaban.

misconceptions.text: Arabic letters keep one shape wherever they appear in a word.
Short vowels are always written, so they can be read directly from every text.
ع, ح and ق are just variants of English sounds like a, h and k.

concepts.name: Attached possessive pronouns
concepts.summary: Attach suffixes such as -ī, -ka, -hu, -hā to nouns to express possession.

concepts.name: Case endings and tanwin
concepts.summary: Recognise the three cases marked by -u, -a, -i and the indefinite tanwin endings.

concepts.name: Independent pronouns and demonstratives
concepts.summary: Use independent pronouns and this/that words with correct gender and number.

concepts.name: Nominal sentence structure
concepts.summary: Build verbless sentences such as al-bayt kabīr, with a definite subject and an indefinite predicate and no verb for 'is'.

concepts.name: Noun gender and agreement
concepts.summary: Make adjectives agree with nouns in gender, number and definiteness.

concepts.name: Sound plurals and dual
concepts.summary: Form the dual with -ān/-ayn and sound masculine and feminine plurals with -ūn/-īn and -āt.

concepts.name: Prepositions and sentence use
concepts.summary: Use common prepositions and recall that they put the following noun in the genitive.

concepts.name: Three-letter root concept
concepts.summary: Identify the root of simple words and see how related words share a core of consonants and meaning.

misconceptions.text: Arabic needs a verb meaning 'is' in every sentence.
Adjectives agree with the noun only in gender.
Case endings are optional decoration that never affect grammar.

concepts.name: Idafa construct phrase
concepts.summary: Build noun-noun possessives in which the first noun loses al- and tanwin and the second noun is genitive.

concepts.name: Past tense conjugation
concepts.summary: Conjugate Form I verbs in the past tense with suffixes for person, gender and number.

concepts.name: Present tense and moods
concepts.summary: Conjugate the present with prefixes and suffixes and distinguish the indicative, subjunctive and jussive endings.

concepts.name: Verbal sentence word order
concepts.summary: Form verb-first sentences in which the verb agrees in gender but stays singular before a plural subject.

concepts.name: Broken plural patterns
concepts.summary: Identify common broken plural patterns, such as afʿāl and fuʿūl, and relate them to the singular's root.

concepts.name: Derivation from roots with patterns
concepts.summary: Analyse how patterns like kātib, maktūb and maktab derive agent, patient and place words from a root.

concepts.name: Negation and particles
concepts.summary: Choose the correct negator for tense and sentence type and apply its effect on the verb or predicate.

concepts.name: Numbers and counted nouns
concepts.summary: Use numbers 1–10 with counted nouns, including the reversed gender agreement of 3–10 and the plural noun.

misconceptions.text: The first noun in an idafa takes al- when the phrase is definite.
A verb before its subject must agree in number as well as gender.
Broken plurals follow no patterns and must be memorised word by word.

concepts.name: Derived verb forms II-X
concepts.summary: Analyse the patterns of Forms II–X and the typical meaning shifts such as causative, reciprocal or reflexive.

concepts.name: Weak and hamzated roots
concepts.summary: Predict how roots with و, ي or hamza change in conjugation, as in qāla and wajada.

concepts.name: Verbal nouns masdar
concepts.summary: Derive and use the verbal noun for each form and analyse its role in clauses and idafa.

concepts.name: Participles and their functions
concepts.summary: Form active and passive participles and analyse their use as nouns, adjectives and predicates.

concepts.name: Passive voice
concepts.summary: Form and interpret the passive through vowel changes and identify the agentless subject.

concepts.name: Relative clauses and subordination
concepts.summary: Join clauses with alladhī and 'anna/inna, and apply the resumptive pronoun rule for definite antecedents.

concepts.name: Inna and kāna sisters
concepts.summary: Evaluate how these particles alter the case of subject and predicate and choose them to express time or emphasis.

concepts.name: Diptotes and case nuance
concepts.summary: Recognise nouns that take no tanwin and only two case forms and explain why.

misconceptions.text: Derived verb forms are unrelated verbs that must be learned separately from the root.
Weak-root verbs are random exceptions rather than predictable sound changes.
Alladhī is used with every relative clause regardless of definiteness.

concepts.name: Diglossia and register choice
concepts.summary: Evaluate when Modern Standard Arabic is appropriate versus spoken dialect and adapt language to context.

concepts.name: Rhetorical style and parallelism
concepts.summary: Assess how rhythm, parallelism and rhetorical devices shape persuasive Arabic prose.

concepts.name: Full vocalisation of unvowelled text
concepts.summary: Infer correct vowels and case endings from root, pattern and syntax in a text with no harakat.

concepts.name: Complex syntax and clause chaining
concepts.summary: Compose and edit long sentences with circumstantial, conditional and subordinate clauses and correct agreement.

concepts.name: Semantic nuance of root derivatives
concepts.summary: Evaluate how different derivatives of one root shade meaning and select the most precise word.

concepts.name: Genre-appropriate writing
concepts.summary: Create original texts in news, academic or literary genres using the conventions, vocabulary and syntax each expects.

concepts.name: Translation and equivalence
concepts.summary: Produce translations that preserve meaning, tone and structure while handling untranslatable idiom and syntax differences.

misconceptions.text: Spoken dialects and Modern Standard Arabic are interchangeable in formal writing.
Good translation means rendering Arabic word by word in the same order.
Words from the same root always mean nearly the same thing.
